title: Separable algebraic closure of a field inside an extension
statement: Let $F\to E$ be a homomorphism of fields, making $E$ an extension of $F$. The *separable algebraic closure of $F$ in $E$* is the set of elements of $E$ that are separable algebraic over $F$ (roots of a separable polynomial with coefficients in $F$); it is a subfield of $E$ containing the image of $F$, and it is algebraic and separable over $F$. If $E$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed] (for instance algebraically closed), then the separable algebraic closure of $F$ in $E$ is separably closed, hence a separable closure of $F$ (a separably closed field, separable algebraic over $F$).

source.place: Lemma Tag 09HC (lemma-separable-elements: the elements of $E$ separable over $k$ form a subextension) and Lemma Tag 09HB (lemma-separable-permanence: separable algebraic over separable algebraic is separable algebraic, which gives that the subextension is separably closed when $E$ is); used with $E=\Omega$ algebraically closed in etale-cohomology.tex Lemma Tag 04HX ('the separable algebraic closure of $\kappa$ in $\kappa(\overline{s})$')

mathlib_searches.query: separable closure of a field inside an algebraically closed extension is separably closed
relative separable closure of F in E is a separable closure when E is separably closed
